---
title: Book projects
---

## Overview

A `book` project renders a set of chapters as a single, numbered work:
chapters and appendices number automatically, cross-references resolve
across chapter boundaries, and citations merge into one book-wide
bibliography. It reuses the `website` project's sidebar navigation: a
table of contents down the side, chapter by chapter.

```bash
q2 create project book mybook
```

```default
Created project in mybook:

  created  _quarto.yml
  created  index.qmd
  created  intro.qmd
  created  summary.qmd
  created  references.qmd
  created  references.json
  created  cover.png
  created  .gitignore

To render it: q2 render mybook
```

The scaffold is a starting point you edit: an unnumbered Preface
(`index.qmd`), an `Introduction` chapter, a `Summary` chapter, and an
unnumbered `References` chapter, plus a `cover.png` and a starter
bibliography.

## `_quarto.yml` shape

```yaml
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "My Book"
  author: "Norah Jones"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - intro.qmd
    - summary.qmd
  references: references.qmd

bibliography: references.json
filters:
  - citeproc
```

`book.chapters` lists the files to render, in book order. The first
entry named `index.*` becomes the book's home page automatically,
wherever it appears in the list. A chapter is numbered unless its
front-matter `title:` or its first heading carries the `.unnumbered`
class — the scaffold's Preface uses this to stay out of the chapter
count:

```markdown
# Preface {.unnumbered}
```

`book.references` names the one chapter that holds the merged
bibliography's `{#refs}` div, numbered in the same sequence as
`book.chapters` — so, like the scaffold's References chapter, it's
usually marked `.unnumbered` too.

### Parts and appendices

Group chapters under a titled divider using `part`:

```yaml
book:
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - part: "Part I: Getting Started"
      chapters:
        - installation.qmd
        - quickstart.qmd
```

Parts nest one level only — a `part:` entry cannot contain another
`part:` entry.

`book.appendices` is a second, separate chapter list that numbers
independently (rendered as letters — Appendix A, B, …) and appears
under its own "Appendices" divider in the sidebar:

```yaml
book:
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - intro.qmd
  appendices:
    - installation-details.qmd
```

## Output formats

Which format you render to changes how chapters combine:

- **HTML** (the default) renders each chapter as its own page —
  `intro.qmd` becomes `intro.html`, and so on — with chapter-aware
  numbering, and cross-references and citations resolved across the
  whole project.
- **Typst and EPUB** merge every chapter into a single document before
  compiling, so `q2 render mybook --to typst` produces one PDF and
  `--to epub` produces one `.epub`; the target format itself keeps
  chapter numbering continuous across the book, rather than restarting
  per chapter the way HTML does.

  Render to Typst without configuring an explicit extension, and Quarto
  auto-resolves to the bundled `orange-book` extension — the same
  zero-config default Quarto 1 uses — so `q2 render mybook --to typst`
  works out of the box. You can configure a *different* Typst book
  extension explicitly; only `orange-book` auto-loads on its own.
- **DOCX, PPTX, and LaTeX** are not supported book targets. DOCX and
  PPTX fail with a clear [`Q-5-33`](../../errors/project/Q-5-33.qmd)
  diagnostic naming the problem rather than silently rendering
  chapters as unrelated documents. LaTeX/PDF book output isn't
  implemented at all yet — Quarto 2 has no LaTeX output for any
  project type, not just books.

## Known limitations

Book projects are new in this release. A few gaps are worth knowing
about up front, rather than discovering them mid-project:

- **Per-chapter front matter beyond the title is dropped in multi-file
  HTML.** A chapter's `subtitle`, `author`, `date`, and `abstract`
  fields don't render — only the book-level versions of these fields
  do.
- **Numeric citation styles renumber independently per chapter in
  multi-file HTML.** The bibliography itself merges correctly across
  chapters, but a numeric CSL style (`[1]`, `[2]`, …) numbers each
  chapter's in-text citations starting from its own count, not one
  continuous sequence across the book. Author-date styles are
  unaffected. (Single-file Typst/EPUB output doesn't have this
  limitation — the whole book is one document there.)
- **No incremental rebuilds.** Every render processes every chapter;
  there's no caching of unchanged chapters yet.
- **Every chapter's data is held in memory for the whole render**,
  for both single-file merge and multi-file HTML. This is fine at the
  scale of a typical book; it hasn't been verified at 50+ chapters.
- **A duplicate cross-reference ID across chapters previews cleanly**
  — `q2 preview` lets the first chapter in book order win, non-fatally
  — **but is a hard error on a real render.** A real duplicate can
  look fine while you're editing and only surface once you render.
- **Cross-chapter reference resolution in `q2 preview` is
  approximate** and recomputed on every preview, adding latency on top
  of the editor's own per-file analysis. It's uncached and unverified
  at large book sizes.
- **Preview shows neither a merged bibliography nor a single-file
  merge.** `q2 preview` always shows one chapter as ordinary HTML, so
  it can't show a Typst/EPUB single-file render or the merged,
  book-wide bibliography.
- **Multi-file HTML doesn't write all chapters atomically.** Chapters
  are written to disk one at a time as rendering proceeds. If a later
  chapter fails, the render still reports failure overall — it isn't
  silent — but an earlier chapter already on disk may reference
  content from the chapter that failed, leaving stale output until the
  next full re-render.
